item.title: pur: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

pur bundles a copy of pip 23.2.1 in pur/packages. That copy has certifi 2023.5.7, with the file pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem. pur puts pur/packages first in sys.path. Thus the bundled requests reads this file for all HTTPS connections. The file has 141 certificates. 24 of them are not in cacert, and 18 are in cacert but not for TLS. The file contains the roots AAA Certificate Services and emSign ECC Root CA - G3. This change replaces the file with a symlink to ${cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt in postInstall. The rm command stops the build when a new version moves the file.

[!NOTE] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description, through patchix. Claude Code used Claude Opus 5.5. A person examined the work before this pull request. This pull request description is written in ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), examined with memelint in strict mode.

Test

nix-cacert-harness examines the package before and after this change. A local copy of nixpkgs is not necessary.

nix run github:irgolic/nix-cacert-harness -- pur --pr 578141 --emudhra
Output of harness: pur 
[1/2] static check + eMudhra chains: offline, reproducible
base (before) = dac5e22db3ed2be013da0eba8050c05140bd3f30
reference: fprs4zi8r6227x12qbsd1grvfrpz6201-nss-cacert-3.131.1 TLS roots=118 all=169
==================================================================
ATTR pur
before: dac5e22db3ed2be013da0eba8050c05140bd3f30   after: worktree <worktree>
before ok (0 built, 1s)
        drv /nix/store/sjf52dlkjzjqqhpjh8z5mdjc2g51wy6c-pur-7.4.0.drv
after  ok (0 built, 1s)
        drv /nix/store/zg88gbgkjsf13w04acvn35qwx4hszh2c-pur-7.4.0.drv

| output:path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| out:/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem 141 certs: 24 not in cacert, 18 in cacert but not for TLS, 19 cacert TLS roots missing; scanner: AAA,ECC G3 | symlink->cacert:ca-bundle.crt pem 169 certs (118 TLS roots + 51 non-TLS, i.e. cacert's own trust-rules bundle) |

inside archives (scanner only; a symlink in the installed output cannot reach them, issue #576542 class):
  before dist:/pur-7.4.0-py3-none-any.whl!pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem  roots=136 trusts AAA Certificate Services,emSign ECC Root CA - C3,emSign ECC Root CA - G3,emSign Root CA - C1,emSign Root CA - G1
  after  dist:/pur-7.4.0-py3-none-any.whl!pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem  roots=136 trusts AAA Certificate Services,emSign ECC Root CA - C3,emSign ECC Root CA - G3,emSign Root CA - C1,emSign Root CA - G1

cacert in runtime closure (before): no
cacert in runtime closure (after): yes
CAs trusted before but not trusted for TLS by cacert (42 total), e.g.:
  - C=GB, O=Comodo CA Limited, CN=AAA Certificate Services
  - C=IN, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Technologies Limited, CN=emSign ECC Root CA - G3
  - C=US, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Inc, CN=emSign ECC Root CA - C3
  - C=US, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Inc, CN=emSign Root CA - C1
  - C=AT, O=e-commerce monitoring GmbH, CN=GLOBALTRUST 2020
  - C=BE, O=GlobalSign nv-sa, OU=Root CA, CN=GlobalSign Root CA
  - C=BM, O=QuoVadis Limited, CN=QuoVadis Root CA 2
  - C=BM, O=QuoVadis Limited, CN=QuoVadis Root CA 3
  - C=CH, O=SwissSign AG, CN=SwissSign Gold CA - G2
  - C=CH, O=SwissSign AG, CN=SwissSign Silver CA - G2
VERDICT pur: FIXED: before trusted CAs outside cacert; after: 1 store(s) == cacert, none with extra CAs (+ bundles inside archives remain, see above)

eMudhra chains (--emudhra; offline and reproducible): the 14 chains in fixtures/emudhra,
each leaf verified against each store (openssl verify -purpose sslserver, at 2026-10-23):
| output:path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| out:/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) | symlink->cacert:ca-bundle.crt pem: accepted 0/14 |
inside archives (zip members, extracted):
| dist:/pur-7.4.0-py3-none-any.whl!pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) |
VERDICT pur emudhra: FIXED: before accepted 14/14 compromised eMudhra chains (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2); after 0/14 (+ after-side archive members accept 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2), see table)

[2/2] live eMudhra test hosts: needs network, NOT reproducible offline
(no shims/pur.{nix,sh} or shims/live/pur.{nix,sh}: live check skipped)

Before the change, the bundled file accepts 14 of the 14 eMudhra chains. It accepts 7 of 7 for emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and 7 of 7 for AAA Certificate Services. After the change, the file is a symlink to the cacert bundle, and it accepts none of the 14 chains. The harness did not do the live test, because it has no shim for pur. The dist output keeps the wheel with the bundled file. pur does not read that wheel.

item.title: linux: patch skb_zerocopy() to propagate the shared-frag marker
item.description:
The kernel just had several vulnerabilities accidentally posted to the public mailing list. Most of them can be mitigated by blacklisting kernel modules or blocking their autoload, except ZDI-CAN-33367, the network code local privilege escalation. The patches have not yet landed in a kernel release; this PR adds the most critical one.

[!NOTE] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description. Claude Code used Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. I examined all of this work. This pull request description is written in ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), examined with memelint in strict mode.

This change adds the upstream patch net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy() to the Linux kernels of nixpkgs. skb_zerocopy() copies the frags of one skb into a different skb, but it does not copy the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag. Thus, ESP input does not identify these frags as shared frags, and it writes the decrypted data into the same frags. Through nfnetlink_queue or an openvswitch upcall, an unprivileged user can write into the page cache of a read-only file that only root can change. The patch is on the netdev list with Cc: stable, but no kernel release has it at this time. This change adds the patch to linux_6_1, linux_6_6, linux_6_12, linux_6_18, linux_7_2, linux_7_3, linux_zen, linux_xanmod, linux_xanmod_stable and linux_xanmod_latest. For linux_7_3, fetchpatch gets the upstream patch. The other kernels do not have the from->unreadable check after the loop that copies the frags. Thus, they get skb-zerocopy-shared-frag-pre-7.3.patch, which has the same change, but the lines around it are different. linux_7_3 builds correctly on x86_64-linux.

Test

linux_7_3 builds correctly on x86_64-linux, and the patch applies without fuzz. I also applied the pre-7.3 patch with patch -p1 --dry-run to net/core/skbuff.c of each of the other kernels. The patch applies without fuzz to each kernel:

  • linux_6_1 (6.1.190): offset -507 lines
  • linux_6_6 (6.6.160): offset -234 lines
  • linux_6_12 (6.12.114): offset -12 lines
  • linux_6_18 (6.18.58): no offset
  • linux_7_2 (7.2.12): offset 51 lines
  • linux_zen (7.2.11-zen1): offset 51 lines
  • linux_xanmod (6.18.58-xanmod1): no offset
  • linux_xanmod_stable and linux_xanmod_latest (7.2.12-xanmod1): offset 51 lines

item.title: jetbrains-jdk: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

nixpkgs builds the JetBrains Runtime, jetbrains.jdk and jetbrains.jdk-no-jcef, from source with dontConfigure = true in pkgs/development/compilers/jetbrains-jdk/common.nix. Thus, the preConfigure step of openjdk, which makes lib/security/cacerts from cacert (#576518), is not done. Before this change, the Java trust store, lib/openjdk/lib/security/cacerts, has the list of JetBrains: 109 roots, and AAA Certificate Services and emSign ECC Root CA - G3 are two of them. This change makes a new cacerts from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts in buildPhase. Then it adds --with-cacerts-file for this file to the options that the mkimages_*.sh script of JetBrains gives to configure. The log of configure shows checking for cacerts file... /build/cacerts-gen/cacerts. After this change, the trust store has 118 roots, the same roots as cacert. The two packages build in the Nix sandbox: jetbrains.jdk-no-jcef in 14 minutes, and jetbrains.jdk in 15 minutes. jetbrains.jdk-21 and jetbrains.jdk-no-jcef-21 use the same common.nix and get the same change, but the harness did not examine them.

item.title: jabref: generate truststore.jks from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

JabRef has a bundled Java trust store, jablib/src/main/resources/ssl/truststore.jks. At start, jabgui and jabkit copy this file to ~/.local/share/jabref/ssl/truststore.jks when there is no copy. Then JabRef uses this copy together with the trust store of its JRE. This change replaces the file in postPatch with a trust store that jre-generate-cacerts makes from the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert, with the password changeit of JabRef. The build puts the file into share/java/jabref/resources/main/ssl and into the four -all.jar files in lib. A user who has a copy keeps the previous trust store, because JabRef copies the file only when there is no copy.

The tokenizers libraries in the .jar files are for macOS and Windows only, and this change does not change them. In the second part of the output, a small Java test on the JRE of JabRef uses TrustStoreManager.createTruststoreFileIfNotExist, as the launchers do. item.title: graalvm-ce: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

GraalVM CE, graalvmPackages.graalvm-ce, is a binary JDK with a bundled Java trust store, lib/security/cacerts. This trust store has 111 certificates, and 33 of them are not in cacert. This change makes a new cacerts with 118 certificates from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts, as the merged openjdk change #576518 does. The change uses the keytool of the package, and autoPatchelf must patch this keytool before it can operate. Thus, the change sets dontAutoPatchelf = true, and postFixup does autoPatchelf before it makes the new cacerts. graalvm-oracle uses the same buildGraalvm.nix, but the harness did not examine graalvm-oracle.

item.title: rubyPackages.certified: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541.

The certified gem has a bundled CA file, certs/ca-bundle.crt. The last version of the gem is 1.0.0 from 2014-07-19, thus this file is from 2014, and no newer version is available. The only function of the gem is to make Net::HTTP use the CA file of the gem. This change adds a certified entry in pkgs/development/ruby-modules/gem-config/default.nix, which replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postInstall. After this change, that file is the cacert bundle, thus on nixpkgs the gem makes Net::HTTP use cacert, the same decision as for python3Packages.certifi.

In nixpkgs, rubyPackages.kramdown-rfc2629 and the Ruby environment of Discourse include this gem. kramdown-rfc2629 does require 'certified' only when it cannot open the default CA file of OpenSSL and the default CA directory has no PEM files. The Gemfile of Discourse has the gem with require: false, and only the tests of Discourse do require "certified", in spec/rails_helper.rb. The change applies to all software that does require "certified". The open pull request #577131 changes the same file for four other gems, and it adds the same cacert argument at the same position. git merge-file merges the two changes with no merge conflict.

item.title: tracecompass: generate the bundled JustJ JRE's cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

Trace Compass, tracecompass, has a bundled JustJ JRE in trace-compass/plugins/org.eclipse.justj.openjdk.*/jre. The Java trust store of this JRE, lib/security/cacerts, has 146 certificates, and 23 of them are not in cacert. This change makes a new cacerts for this JRE from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts and the keytool of jdk21. Trace Compass uses jdk21 and not this JRE, because the package adds a -vm line for jdk21 to tracecompass.ini. Thus, this change has an effect only when a different tool starts the bundled JRE.

The harness tests the package with the 14 certificate chains of the eMudhra incident, from https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ (only the certificates, not the keys). Before this change, the trust store of the bundled JustJ JRE accepts 7 of the 14 chains (accepted 7/14). Thus, it accepts the eMudhra intermediate certificates through emSign ECC Root CA - G3. After this change, the trust store accepts no chain (accepted 0/14). In the second part of the output, a small Java test starts the bundled JustJ JRE. The test sends one request to each of four test servers with HttpsURLConnection and the default trust store. The package does not patch this JRE, thus the test starts its bin/java through the dynamic loader of nixpkgs. Before this change, the test connects to the two servers with the G3 chain. After this change, the test connects to no server. The harness compares the certificates by their SHA-256 fingerprints, because jre-generate-cacerts does not keep the usual aliases.
